api_under_test: Drizzle column in db/schema.ts + guren make:migration (posts.published_at, nullable text)
named model scopes (static scopes = { published, scheduled }) applied with Post.scope() / query.scope(), behind one model-level visibility helper that index, show and search share
where-group callbacks (where((q) => ...) / orWhere / whereNull) so the visibility condition ANDs onto search's keyword group and paginate's count
firstOrFail() on the scoped query for the 404 on another user's scheduled post
this.auth.user<UserRecord>() for the optional viewer on public routes
route body contract: a zod field on PostPayloadSchema (z.iso.datetime / z.coerce.date) so an invalid publishAt gets the same 422 as an invalid title
Command subclass (static signature 'posts:scheduled', handle(), this.line()) registered in src/console.ts's ConsoleKernel, scaffolded by guren make:command --command posts:scheduled
harness_signal: The baseline has no scheduling and no console commands; a column, a migration, the model, the validator, four controller actions, the resource, four pages and a console command all move. `guren context` lists scope(name) in the QueryBuilder chain and the app's console commands; `guren make:command X --command posts:scheduled` writes the class and registers it in src/console.ts, and `guren check` warns about a command class no kernel registers. Nothing in check or audit notices a visibility rule applied to one action and forgotten on another, so the three-way consistency (index, show, search) is guidance only. Traps for the unaided: a top-level orWhere('authorId', …) that ORs past search's keyword group or the list's other conditions; this.info()/success() in the command, which prefixes every line and breaks the pinned output; a bin/ script or console.log that bypasses the kernel; storing the form value unnormalized, so string comparison against an ISO now stops meaning time order; and mass assignment, since Post.update() throws on a key missing from fillable. The shipped+plan condition hands the agent the approved plan's steps, starting with the make:command generator.

plan_authoring.notes: Written by an Opus authoring subagent inside its task-authoring session (no separate spend). About 5 min reading the implementation-plans guide, plan/schema.ts, the column/field type judgement in plan/status.ts and field-status.ts, and post-tags' plan; about 4 min writing, one plan:render (clean apart from the standing 'validators could not be read' warn), plan:approve at the baseline, and the harness plan:next check in a second worktree, which returned task/foundation/commands. A second pass (about 2 min) added AC-12/AC-13 on posts.create and posts.edit: without a behaviour on those routes nothing reaches view.posts.new or view.posts.edit (in cli 2.27.0 a view's form.submitsTo carries no behaviour, an action's response.view does), so the pages step could not lift them; the plan was re-approved from scratch in a fresh baseline worktree and plan:next re-checked. The schema has no element for a console command or a query scope: the command is a plan `commands` entry (guren make:command ScheduledPosts --command posts:scheduled, allowed as a make:* generator), and the scopes, the shared visibility helper and the command's output format are assumptions plus action rules. published_at is typed `string` rather than `datetime`, since plan:status reads a SQLite text column as ambiguous for datetime and would never match it. The validator is written for z.iso.datetime({ offset: true }).nullish(), a form plan:status can read. The altered actions and views stay unjudged until their behaviours verify, as the guide describes for an alter whose planned properties already held.
